component.name: Kite
component.summary: KDE web browser with Firefox extension support

description.p: Kite is a web browser for the Plasma desktop, modelled on Falkon and written in Rust. It runs Firefox extensions, installed straight from addons.mozilla.org.

It blocks ads and trackers itself, keeps passwords in KWallet, fills forms, has a reader view, container tabs, and private windows that leave nothing behind. Plugins add Vim keys, mouse gestures, picture-in-picture, and integration with Plasma: media controls, KRunner, KDE Connect and the panel's download progress.

screenshot.caption: Kite on Plasma, showing its empty start page

description.p: The sliding of the sidebar and the docked developer tools can be switched off in Settings, under Appearance. It stays on unless you change it.
The bookmarks and history sidebar slides in when you open it and out when you close it, like the docked developer tools, and reopens at the width you last gave it.
Developer tools docked beside the page slide in when you open them and out when you close them, following your system's animation speed.
Hardening for extensions: a content script can no longer tell its extension's background page that it is the popup or another site, and extensions never share a script world.
Printing works in the Flatpak. A print job ended with "Printing needs CUPS' lp command", because the Flatpak has no such command; Kite now uses the one it has.
Sites behind a bot check let Kite in: xdaforums.com no longer keeps it at "Hold tight", and forbes.com shows no captcha. Kite did not tell sites which languages you read, as every browser does.
Settings → Browsing has "Languages for pages": your system's languages unless you list your own.
Tabs can be sent to a saved session: a tab's menu sends it, or the tabs selected, to a session or a new one, and a group's menu the whole group. They open again with that session.
Drag a tab away from the tab bar, or out of the window, and it gets a window of its own. In split view, drag a tab onto the other side's tabs or its page to move it there.
With Vim keys, f finds its links on very long pages too, where it used to say there was nothing to follow.
A security update, from a review of Kite's own code. Updating is recommended.

A web page could reach Kite's own pages, and through them its settings. A saved login or address could be filled into another page than the one it was for. An extension allowed on one site could act on others, and read what was meant for another extension. Text from pages and add-ons was drawn as markup in tooltips, menus and lists. All of this is put right.

A proxy set in Settings is now used for everything Kite fetches itself (filter lists, search suggestions, add-ons), not only for pages. A private window started with --private leaves nothing behind when Kite crashes.
Some extensions have to say what they use: listening to requests, notifications, menus and a few more now take the permission for it in the manifest, as in Firefox.
Save Page As (Ctrl+S) on a PDF document, a picture, a video or text saves the file itself under its own name. It used to offer an .html file.

More extensions work. Those that call browser.* with callbacks now get their answers; the Unhook add-on for YouTube takes effect and keeps its settings. Extensions that send a page elsewhere are told the right tab. An extension can put its own script into pages that require Trusted Types, such as YouTube.
The toolbar can have a Profiles button: add it in Customize Toolbar. It shows the picture of the profile you are in and opens the Profiles menu.

Password manager extensions work much better, Bitwarden among them. Their entries are on the right-click menu, with submenus complete. Their menu inside login fields appears. Passkeys kept in the extension can be made and used: the request no longer waits forever, and the extension asks in a small window of its own. An extension's popup takes the keyboard as it opens, closes with Escape, and can close itself. Copying works from an extension's sidebar, tab and window as it did from its popup. An extension's scripts no longer stop working once its popup has been opened and closed.

Extensions are kept apart more strictly. One extension no longer hears of the requests another extension's own pages make, which could give away what identifies that extension to Kite. What a content script may ask of Kite is now limited to messaging, storage and a few facts about where it runs, as in Firefox, wherever the call comes from: an extension's session storage is for its own pages unless the extension opens it to its content scripts.

Parental controls: a profile can be a child's. It blocks adult sites by community-kept lists, holds search engines to their safe search, can't install extensions or plugins, and can't be left for another profile without the parent password. Set up in the profile picker or in Settings, under Parental Controls. This works inside Kite; a system account of the child's own is what holds beyond that.

The profile picker shows the profiles as cards, and each profile can have a picture: choose an image, then move and zoom it into place. The Profiles menu shows the pictures too. The default profile can now be renamed.

Fixes a crash: when a page had opened another page in a tab or popup window and the opening tab was closed, moving the pointer over the opened page crashed Kite. Extensions are now told that they run in Firefox, which is what they are made for (Settings, Plugins and Extensions; on by default). What Kite fetches itself, such as extensions' requests, add-ons and filter lists, now trusts the certificate authorities of your system, so an extension can reach a self-hosted server with a certificate authority of its own.

An extension's popup stays open when the extension changes its toolbar button. Before, it closed, which cut Bitwarden's login short: the account then showed as locked and could not be unlocked ("KDF parameters are required"). If yours is in that state, log out on the lock screen and log in again.

Web apps run faster: the scripts Kite adds to every page for its content blocker, saved logins and autofill, overlay scrollbars, link pings and pointer lock no longer slow down the page's own work (Speedometer 3.1 went from about 23.7 to about 26.8 on the same engine). With the Vim keys plugin on, pages get the key releases they send themselves again, which some web apps rely on. "Block link click pings" is now the engine's own switch: unticked, such pings are really sent. The AppImage now comes with QtWebEngine 6.140, with Chromium's security fixes up to version 157.

PDF documents open in the tab, in the engine's own viewer, where they used to be downloaded; a setting under Browsing has them downloaded instead. The downloads button's panel now lists the downloads that have just ended, the ones its dot is about, with Open, Show in folder and Remove from list.

Open tabs use less memory: about 10 MiB less each in Kite itself, as a tab's menus, prompts and popups are made when first needed, and about 4 MiB less per page, as pages are no longer gone through for scrollbars of their own. A scrollbar a page draws itself now gets the overlay look when pointed at or scrolled. A performance report against Falkon and Firefox is in the documentation.

Page Info: a window with a page's technical details and meta tags, its pictures and media to preview and save (one by one or all at once), every permission its site can be given, and its connection, history and cookies. The address bar's site popup now lists only the permissions a site is allowed or is using.

A site allowed or blocked from opening links like mailto: is no longer asked about again after a restart. Show in Folder no longer freezes Kite or opens a second file manager when the file manager is slow to start; the Flatpak asks the file manager directly, for which it may now talk to org.freedesktop.FileManager1.

Fixes a crash when a tab's icon was drawn after tabs had been unloaded, dropdowns on pages closing at once on Wayland, and the tab crashing on Line wrap in a page's source. The Library keeps its lists and bars inside a narrow window, and history has a new icon.

Show in Folder opens the file manager with the downloaded file selected. In the settings, the spell checking languages and the search engines are lists like the saved logins, with a button to remove each entry and one to remove all.

The downloads button opens a panel with the downloads under way, which can be paused and cancelled there; the full list moved into the Library. Toolbar buttons are all as tall as the address bar and stay pressed in while their menu is open.
The custom rules in the Content Blocking settings can be scrolled, so rules past the end of the field can be reached.
A possible fix for Vim keys, and a site's own keyboard shortcuts, doing nothing on a newly opened page while an input method such as IBus is running.
The Flatpak follows the desktop's colors when they change while Kite is open, such as a switch between a light and a dark theme.
The extensions button's panel leaves out the Extensions section while WebExtensions are switched off.
The About dialog shows Kite's icon again.
Kite as a Flatpak, from a repository that keeps it updated. Its application ID is now io.github.n4n0gh.kite.

Private windows can have purple window chrome. Vim keys no longer go quiet with the keyboard in a widget frame or a picker. Profiles can be renamed from the picker. A YouTube Download plugin saves videos with yt-dlp. The built-in blocker works like uBlock Origin, with an element picker.
Settings laid out as in System Settings, with Apply. A user agent per site. A log file and crash reports. Forms act only on trusted clicks, submits and Enter.
Pointer lock for pages, on Wayland.
